_comment: Project permissions. Checked in on purpose: every session and every worktree
inherits these, so nobody configures anything and nobody drifts.
GOAL: silence for the things this project does a hundred times a day, and a
stop for the small number of things that are destructive or irreversible.
This is deliberately NOT bypassPermissions. That mode is documented for
isolated containers without internet access, and this repository is the
opposite of that: it holds live Cloudflare deploy credentials, it can push to
a production instance, and its whole job is to fetch and parse UNTRUSTED
documents from the public web. Adversarial text inside a captured page is a
real vector here in a way it is not for most projects, and the bash gate is
what stands between that text and the shell.
If a command you run often still prompts, choose the don't-ask-again option
once. That approval saves to .claude/settings.local.json in the main checkout
and applies in every worktree, so it is a one-time cost. Then add it here so
the next session inherits it too.
